mainTopic: Which work is allowed on חול המועד: מעשה הדיוט versus מעשה אומן, field work judged by intention, and business permitted only to prevent a loss
overview: This amud gives a long list of rulings about which work is allowed on חול המועד. It starts with jobs connected to mills and animals. רב יהודה and רבא permit several of these, and אביי brings a ברייתא that supports רבא's ruling that an animal may be given medical care. Next comes a key rule: simple work anyone can do (מעשה הדיוט) is allowed, but skilled craftsman's work (מעשה אומן) is forbidden. רבא then gives four field rulings: leveling ground, clearing twigs, letting water into a field, and cutting palm branches. Each one is allowed for a present, non-farming purpose and forbidden if it is done to improve the land, and the גמרא gives a visible sign for telling the two apart. Finally, the גמרא rules that business is forbidden on חול המועד unless there would be a real loss (דבר האבד). It illustrates this with stories about רבינא, and it begins a ברייתא about עבודה זרה that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No hoof-trimming for a mill donkey
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier statement: the hooves of a donkey that turns a millstone are not trimmed on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a donkey that turns the mill: no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement that began just before this section. It says that the hoof-trimming allowed for other animals does not apply to a mill donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Trimming hooves was allowed for some animals on חול המועד. This line carves out one case that does not get that permission: the donkey that turns the mill.

keyTerms.meaning: A donkey that turns a millstone
The intermediate days of a festival (חול המועד)

phrases.english: But a donkey of the mill — no.
phrases.notes: This finishes a statement from just before. It means the mill donkey's hooves may not be trimmed on חול המועד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a ruling that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mill donkey's hooves are not trimmed on חול המועד.

steps.title: רב יהודה allows mill-related work
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה permits trimming a mill donkey's hooves, setting up and building a mill, building a mill's water channel, and building a stable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה permits trimming the hooves of a mill donkey, setting up a mill, building a mill, building a mill's water channel, and building a stable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a list of jobs he allows on חול המועד, most of them connected to running a mill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Notice that his first item, trimming a mill donkey's hooves, is the very thing the line before said was not allowed. So רב יהודה takes a more lenient position on this case. The rest of the list adds more work on the mill itself and a stable.

keyTerms.meaning: The water channel that drives a mill

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume רב יהודה is just repeating the line before. That line said a mill donkey is not trimmed; רב יהודה allows it.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda permits
trimming the hooves of the mill donkey,
and setting up a mill, and building a mill,
phrases.notes: Setting up means putting the millstones in place. Building means making the base of the mill.

phrases.english: and building a mill's water channel,
and building a stable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a more lenient ruling on the same mill-donkey case and adds related jobs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mill-related work, including trimming a mill donkey's hooves and building a stable, is allowed on חול המועד.

steps.title: רבא allows grooming a horse and building a trough and bench
steps.stepSummary: רבא permits combing a horse, building a feeding trough, and building a bench.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא permitted combing a horse, building a trough, and building a bench.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another list of permitted jobs, this time from רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are more everyday jobs: caring for a horse and building simple items like a trough or a bench. They join רב יהודה's list as work allowed on חול המועד.

phrases.english: Rava permitted combing a horse,
and building a trough, and building a bench.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more permitted jobs to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grooming a horse and building a trough or a bench are allowed on חול המועד.

steps.title: רבא allows bloodletting for an animal
steps.stepSummary: רבא permits letting blood from an animal on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא permitted letting blood from an animal on חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a ruling about medical care for animals. The next step will bring support for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bloodletting was a medical treatment. רבא allows it for an animal on חול המועד, so taking care of an animal's health is not blocked by the festival.

keyTerms.meaning: To let blood (literally, to take blood)

phrases.english: Rava permitted letting blood from an animal
on the intermediate days of the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling from רבא, this time about animal medicine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bloodletting for an animal is allowed on חול המועד.

steps.title: אביי brings a ברייתא that supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רבא that a ברייתא supports him: animals may have blood let and may get any medical treatment on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: A ברייתא was taught that supports you: We let blood from an animal, and we do not hold back medical treatment from an animal on חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי backs up רבא's ruling by quoting a ברייתא that says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matches רבא's ruling on bloodletting. It also goes further: no medical treatment at all is held back from an animal on חול המועד. So רבא's ruling now rests on an earlier source, not only on his own view.
steps.whatToRemember: Animals may get medical care on חול המועד, including bloodletting. רבא said it, and a ברייתא backs him up.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him,
It was taught in a baraita that supports you:
We let blood from an animal,
and we do not withhold medical treatment from an animal
on the intermediate days of a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's ruling from step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that bloodletting for an animal is allowed on חול המועד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: we let blood from an animal and do not withhold medical treatment from it on חול המועד.

steps.title: רבא allows scrubbing clothes because it is simple work
steps.stepSummary: רבא permits scrubbing garments. The reason: it is מעשה הדיוט, the kind of work anyone can do.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא permitted scrubbing garments. What is the reason? It is simple, unskilled work.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא allows scrubbing clothes on חול המועד, and the גמרא explains why: it is simple work that anyone can do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is the key here. Work that needs no special skill (מעשה הדיוט) is treated more leniently on חול המועד. This sets up the contrast in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Simple work that anyone can do

phrases.english: Rava permitted scrubbing garments.
What is the reason? It is the work of a layman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another רבא ruling, this time with a stated reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scrubbing clothes is allowed on חול המועד because it is מעשה הדיוט.

steps.title: רב חסדא forbids tying pleats in sleeves because it is skilled work
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, quoted by רב יצחק בר אמי, forbids tying sleeves into pleats on חול המועד because it is מעשה אומן, skilled work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר אמי said in the name of רב חסדא: Tying sleeves into pleats is forbidden. What is the reason? It is skilled craftsman's work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposite case. Tying pleats into sleeves is forbidden on חול המועד because it takes a craftsman's skill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Put next to step 6, this gives a clear rule. Simple work (מעשה הדיוט) is allowed and skilled work (מעשה אומן) is forbidden. Both are clothing jobs, so the only difference is the level of skill needed.
steps.whatToRemember: On חול המועד, simple work anyone can do (מעשה הדיוט) is allowed, but skilled craftsman's work (מעשה אומן) is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between מעשה הדיוט and מעשה אומן is a basic test for deciding which work is allowed on חול המועד.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַמֵּי אֲמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Ami said that Rav Chisda said:
Tying sleeves into pleats is forbidden.
What is the reason? It is the work of a craftsman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַמֵּי אֲמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite case to step 6: skilled clothing work, which is forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tying pleats in sleeves is forbidden on חול המועד because it is מעשה אומן.

steps.title: Leveling the ground: threshing floor versus farmland
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that leveling the ground on חול המועד is permitted if it is done to make a threshing floor. It is forbidden if it is done to improve the land for planting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If someone levels the ground with the intention of making a threshing floor, it is permitted. If he does it with the intention of improving the land, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new rule: leveling the ground depends on why you are doing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The physical act is the same in both cases: smoothing out the ground. What decides the הלכה is the goal. Preparing a threshing floor is allowed, but preparing the land itself for farming is forbidden on חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: Levels or smooths out the ground
With the intention of; for the purpose of

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a pattern that repeats in רבא's next several rulings (twigs, water, date palm): the person's purpose decides whether a field act is allowed on חול המועד.

phrases.english: Rava said:
One who levels the ground
with the intention of a threshing floor, it is permitted;
with the intention of the land, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: 'For the land' means fixing up the soil itself so it is better for planting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling by רבא in the series of חול המועד rulings from steps 3–7, now about field work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leveling the ground on חול המועד is permitted for a threshing floor and forbidden for improving farmland.

steps.title: How to tell which purpose the leveler has
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we can tell the two cases apart. Moving dirt from mound to mound, or from furrow to furrow, shows he wants a threshing floor. Moving dirt from a mound into a furrow shows he is fixing the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? Mound into mound, and furrow into furrow, shows he is making a threshing floor. If he took dirt from a mound and threw it into a furrow, he is fixing the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the practical case and answers it: the way the dirt is moved reveals the purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Intention alone is invisible, so the גמרא gives an outward sign. Piling dirt onto other mounds or into other furrows clears a space without flattening the whole field. Filling furrows with dirt from mounds evens out the land itself, which is farming work.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look in practice?
A mound or raised bump of earth
A furrow or low groove in the ground

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא simply trusts whatever the person says his intention is. The גמרא gives a visible test based on how the dirt is moved.

phrases.english: What is the case?
Mound onto mound
and furrow into furrow
is with the intention of a threshing floor;
if he took a mound and threw it into a furrow,
that is with the intention of the land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies how to recognize the two intentions in רבא's rule from step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can an observer tell whether the leveling is for a threshing floor or for the land?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Mound to mound or furrow to furrow means a threshing floor. Mound into furrow means fixing the land.

steps.title: Clearing twigs: firewood versus farmland
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that clearing twigs from a field on חול המועד is permitted if he wants the wood. It is forbidden if he is clearing the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: If someone gathers twigs with the intention of using the wood, it is permitted. If he does it with the intention of clearing the land, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second ruling built the same way as the first, this time about gathering twigs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, one physical act can have two purposes. Collecting wood for use is fine, but clearing the field to prepare it for planting is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Wood, sticks (for use, such as firewood)

phrases.english: And Rava said:
One who clears twigs,
with the intention of the wood, it is permitted;
with the intention of the land, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הַאי מַאן דְּזָכֵי זִיכֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling by רבא that applies the same intention-based logic as step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gathering twigs on חול המועד is permitted for the wood and forbidden for clearing the land.

steps.title: How to tell which purpose the twig-gatherer has
steps.stepSummary: Taking only the big twigs and leaving the small ones shows he wants wood. Taking both big and small shows he is clearing the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he takes the big ones and leaves the small ones, he wants the wood. If he takes both big and small ones, he is clearing the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא again asks for the practical case and gives a visible sign of his intention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who wants wood takes only pieces worth using. Someone who also picks up the tiny useless bits must be trying to clean the ground itself, which is farming work.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If he takes the big ones and leaves the small ones,
that is with the intention of the wood;
if he took big ones and small ones,
phrases.notes: The small twigs are not useful as wood, so taking them shows he wants a clean field.

phrases.english: that is with the intention of the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? שָׁקֵיל רַבְרְבֵי וְשָׁבֵיק זוּטְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies how to recognize the two intentions in רבא's twig ruling from step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can an observer tell whether the twigs are gathered for wood or to clear the land?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only big twigs means he wants wood. Big and small together means he is clearing the land.

steps.title: Letting water into a field: fish versus watering the land
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that opening a water channel into one's land on חול המועד is permitted if it is done to catch fish. It is forbidden if it is done to water the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: If someone opens water into his land with the intention of catching fish, it is permitted. If he does it with the intention of watering the land, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third ruling built the same way: letting water into a field depends on the purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Opening the channel looks the same either way. If he wants the fish that come in with the water, it is allowed. If he wants to water the field for farming, it is forbidden. The next step gives the visible test for telling the two apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Opened water, such as a channel

steps.whatToRemember: All three of רבא's rulings so far follow one pattern. A field act done for a permitted, non-farming purpose (a threshing floor, wood, or fish) is allowed on חול המועד. The same act done to improve the land is forbidden. For each one, the גמרא shows how to tell the purpose from what the person actually does. The next step gives that sign for the water case.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
One who opens water into his land,
with the intention of fish, it is permitted;
with the intention of the land, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הַאי מַאן דְּפָתַח מַיָּא לְאַרְעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third parallel ruling by רבא, using the same intention-based structure as steps 8 and 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening water into one's land on חול המועד is permitted to catch fish and forbidden to water the land.

steps.title: How to Tell Fishing From Watering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we can tell whether opening the water channel is for fish or for watering the land. The answer: two gates means fish, one gate means watering.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he opens two gates, one at the top and one at the bottom, he wants fish. If he opens only one gate, he wants to water the land.
steps.whatsHappening: Just as it did in Step 9 and Step 11, the גמרא asks how we can see what the person intends, this time for רבא's water-channel ruling from Step 12. It answers with a sign anyone can see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two gates, the water flows in and flows right back out, so the land is not really being watered and only fish are left behind. With one gate, the water stays and soaks the field, so it looks like he is watering his land, which is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look in practice?
Gate / gates (openings in the water channel)

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If he opens two gates,
one above and one below —
phrases.notes: Water comes in one gate and runs out the other, so the field doesn't stay flooded and only the fish remain.

phrases.english: it is with the intention of catching fish;
if he opens one gate —
it is with the intention of watering the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the visible sign that tells apart the two intentions in רבא's water-channel ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can we see whether he opened the channel for fish or for watering?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two gates (one above, one below) means fish; one gate means watering the land.

steps.title: Cutting Palm Branches: For Animals or For the Tree
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that cutting palm branches on חול המועד is permitted to feed animals and forbidden to improve the tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Someone who cuts branches off a date palm is permitted if it is for his animals and forbidden if it is for the palm tree.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives another ruling in the same style as before. The same action can be permitted or forbidden depending on why it is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting animal food is a present need, so it is allowed. Trimming the tree so it grows better is farm work for the future, so it is forbidden on חול המועד.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הַאי מַאן דְּפָשַׁח דִּיקְלָא,
phrases.english: And Rava said: One who cuts branches off a date palm,
if with the intention of feeding his animals — it is permitted;
if with the intention of helping the date palm — it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הַאי מַאן דְּפָשַׁח דִּיקְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling by רבא that follows the same intention-based pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting palm branches is permitted for animal food and forbidden for improving the tree.

steps.title: How to Tell Animal Food From Tree Care
steps.stepSummary: Cutting all the branches from one side shows he wants animal food. Cutting from both sides shows he is caring for the tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he takes everything from one side, it is for the animals. If he takes from this side and that side, it is for the tree, and it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא again asks how we can see what he intends, and it gives a clear sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stripping one side bare does not help the tree, so he obviously just wants the branches. Trimming evenly on both sides is how you shape a tree to grow well, so that shows he is doing farm work.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If he takes all of it from one side —
it is with the intention of feeding his animals;
if from this side and from that side —
it is with the intention of helping the date palm, and it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the visible sign for רבא's palm ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can we see whether he cut the branches for animals or for the tree?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: All from one side means for animals; from both sides means for the tree, which is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: In all of רבא's rulings here, the same action is permitted or forbidden based on intention, and the גמרא always gives an outward sign that shows that intention.

steps.title: Unripe Dates: Cutting Is Fine, Preserving Is Not
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that cutting up unripe dates on חול המועד is permitted, but preserving them is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: These unripe dates may be cut up, but preserving them is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new ruling about unripe dates. Preparing them to eat now is allowed, but processing them for later is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting them up makes them ready to eat during the holiday. Preserving them is for use after the holiday, so it counts as unnecessary work on חול המועד.

phrases.english: And Rava said: These unripe dates —
cutting them up is permitted;
preserving them is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Preserved dates won't be ready until after the holiday, so this is work done for later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another independent ruling by רבא about work on חול המועד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting unripe dates is permitted; preserving them is forbidden.

steps.title: רב פפא Permits Preserving Because They Will Spoil
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says preserving unripe dates is permitted, because they get wormy and would otherwise be lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Since they get wormy, they are like goods that will be lost, and preserving them is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא disagrees with the second half of רבא's ruling and permits preserving the dates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא adds a new fact: the dates will become wormy if they are left alone. That puts them in the category of something that will be lost, and work to prevent a loss is allowed on חול המועד.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Since they become wormy —
they are like merchandise that will be lost, and it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבא's ban on preserving the dates.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Preserving unripe dates is permitted because they would otherwise spoil, so they count as something that will be lost.

steps.title: Any Business Is Forbidden on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that any business at all is forbidden on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Business of any amount is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא moves to a new topic, buying and selling during חול המועד, and gives a broad ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'any amount' mean that even a small deal is forbidden. This sets up the next step, which adds an exception.

keyTerms.meaning: Any amount at all, even a little

phrases.english: And Rava said:
Any business at all is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: פְּרַקְמַטְיָא כָּל שֶׁהוּא, אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: business on חול המועד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any business, even small, is forbidden on חול המועד.

steps.title: Exception: When There Will Be a Loss
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין adds that business is permitted when otherwise there would be a real loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר אבין said: But in a case of a דבר האבד, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר אבין adds an exception to רבא's ban on business.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban covers ordinary business. When waiting would cause a real loss (a דבר האבד), the business is permitted. This matches רב פפא's reasoning about the wormy dates.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that will be lost if not handled now

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin said:
But in a matter that will be lost — it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין: וּבַדָּבָר הָאָבֵד — מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבא's broad ban with an exception for loss.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Business that prevents a real loss is permitted on חול המועד.

steps.title: רבינא Waits and Earns Double
steps.stepSummary: רבינא could have sold his business goods for six thousand during חול המועד. He waited until after the holiday and sold them for twelve thousand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא had some business goods that could sell for six thousand. He waited to sell them until after חול המועד, and he sold them for twelve thousand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רבינא keeping the ban on business during חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא did not treat a chance to sell for six thousand as a reason to sell during the holiday. He held back, and in the end he earned double, which shows that keeping the ban did not cost him.

keyTerms.meaning: חול המועד, the middle days of the holiday

steps.whatToRemember: Business is forbidden on חול המועד except to prevent a real loss. The story of רבינא shows someone waiting rather than selling, and gaining from it.

phrases.english: Ravina had a certain business venture
that could have been sold for six thousand;
he delayed selling it until after the intermediate days of the Festival
and sold it for twelve thousand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story showing the ban on business being kept in practice.

steps.title: רבינא asks about collecting a debt on the holiday
steps.stepSummary: רבינא was owed money by the people of אקרא דשנואתא and asks רב אשי if he may go to collect it now, on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא was owed money by the people of the fortress of אקרא דשנואתא. He came to רב אשי and asked: May I go to them now, during חול המועד, to collect it?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story starts. רבינא asks רב אשי a practical question: may he travel on חול המועד to collect a debt?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that business is forbidden on חול המועד unless there would be a real loss (Step 19). Collecting a debt looks like ordinary business, so רבינא is unsure whether it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Was owed money (literally, 'had coins coming up')
The fortress of Shanvata, a place name

phrases.english: Ravina was owed money
by the people of the fortress of Shanvata.
He came before Rav Ashi.
He said to him: What is the law about going
to them now?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַהוּ לְמֵיזַל הָאִידָּנָא עֲלַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story testing the rule that business is forbidden on חול המועד except to prevent a loss.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may travel on חול המועד to collect a debt.

steps.title: רב אשי permits it because the debt would otherwise be lost
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that since these debtors can only be found now, the case counts like פרקמטיא האבד, so it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: Since you can only find them now, and on other days you cannot find them, this is like business that would be lost, and it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רבינא's question and allows him to go collect the debt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key fact is that these debtors are only around now; at other times he would not find them. So waiting could mean losing the money entirely, which fits the exception of real loss from Step 19. The debt is not truly 'merchandise,' but it is treated like it.

keyTerms.meaning: Business or merchandise that would be lost

steps.whatToRemember: Collecting a debt on חול המועד is permitted when you could not collect it later; it is treated like פרקמטיא האבד.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the 'real loss' exception applies beyond selling goods, including collecting money you would otherwise lose.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב אשי answering רבינא.

phrases.english: Since it is now that you find them,
and on other days you do not find them,
it is like merchandise that would be lost,
and it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question from Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Permitted, because the debtors are only available now, so it counts as preventing a loss.

steps.title: A ברייתא about idol worship follows the same idea
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא about עבודה זרה that works the same way: you may act when there would otherwise be a loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught in a ברייתא about עבודה זרה, in a case like this: One may go...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a supporting source. It starts quoting a ברייתא, which continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'like this case' tell us the ברייתא follows the same reasoning as רב אשי: collecting debts is allowed when they would otherwise be lost. Only the first word of the ברייתא appears here, so the full support comes next.
